A1.justification: Both complete ten-page PDFs describe the same work. Their text, equations, Tables 1–2, Figures 1–10, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Table 2 report original trained-model results for classification, video question answering, tracking, and colorization, alongside generated examples and attention analyses.

after.justification: The original experimental results are retained, and Table 2 additionally reports the proposed model's results on TGIF-QA.

M1.justification: The frame-based task reformulation, transformer architecture, patch merging, causal attention, autoregressive inference, and training loss remain unchanged. The newly stated parameter count documents the existing model rather than establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: Section 3.1 and Table 2 add TGIF-QA's frame question-answering task using animated GIFs. This extends video question answering beyond CLEVRER's synthetic scenes while retaining all existing datasets and task types.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands comparisons: BERT-base on SST-2; ViT-base and Resnet-101 on CIFAR-10; LSTM + Attn on TGIF-QA; Dai et al. on LaSOT; and Zhang et al. and Yang et al. on colorization. Other table baselines already appeared in v1's prose and are retained comparisons.

E3.justification: Figure 10 changes the stated spatial-attention averaging from all encoding layers to all layers, a limited reported analysis-protocol revision; recomputation is not established. Table 1 configurations, training budgets, checkpoint selection, OCR evaluation, and benchmark metrics otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same attention-map cases, short-input SST-2 check, audio digit-confusion analysis, and tracking-error observations are retained. No new ablation, robustness test, or diagnostic evidence is added; Figure 10 changes its display and stated aggregation protocol.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added results do not introduce a new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 substantially expands concrete comparative results across several tasks and adds TGIF-QA scores: PSNR 42.0, SSIM 98.5, F1 53.2, and accuracy 52.3, alongside baseline accuracy 51.9. Existing proposed-model scores are retained; colorization CDC changing from 0.0169 to 0.02 is rounding, not a performance change.

T1.justification: The video and patch definitions and both CDC equations remain unchanged. The condensed metric explanation introduces no new mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: Despite shortened abstract wording and revised conclusion phrasing, the paper retains its central claims: unifying modalities through next-frame prediction without dedicated encoders, achieving comparable non-pretrained single-task performance, and providing a foundation for broader multimodal models.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations concerning text truncation, CLEVRER frame and resolution constraints, autoregressive tracking errors, color diversity versus consistency, and future pretraining remain substantively unchanged. The additional comparisons do not introduce new mechanism explanations or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly discloses the model's 41M parameters, compared with Transframer's 470–829M. Table 2 also explicitly marks baselines pretrained on other datasets. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training-time information, and OCR access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The revision acknowledges Transframer as an earlier attempt to unify visual tasks and adds references supporting TGIF-QA, Dai's tracker, and the Zhang and Yang colorizers. These are limited additions to otherwise retained research positioning; the shortened GPT-4 author list does not remove that work.

P1.justification: Localized edits shorten the abstract, metric explanations, and captions; correct wording such as 'finetuned' to 'trained'; and revise the conclusion's opening. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially redesigned from proposed-model-only results into grouped multi-model comparisons, adding a Model column and pretraining markers. Figures 1, 9, and 10 are reduced in size, Figure 10's color scale moves from below to the side, and surrounding text is reflowed. The illustrated examples are retained.

improvement.justification: TGIF-QA and the additional baselines provide useful evidence for the existing feasibility claim. Table 2's explicit comparisons and pretraining markers, together with the parameter-count disclosure, improve assessment of the work. The gain is limited by sparse documentation of the added evaluations and the reduced legibility of Figure 10; the method and original findings remain unchanged.
